action: Terminated any locked dotnet/apphost/ProjectName* processes, then ran 'dotnet run --project ProjectName.AppHost --no-launch-profile'. After ~25s both resources confirmed live: GET http://localhost:5044/ -> 200 {service:ProjectName.Runtime,...,status:ready}, GET http://localhost:5200/ -> 200 {service:ProjectName.OrchestrationApi,...}.

Called GET http://localhost:5200/api/chat?prompt=... : failed both attempts with HTTP 502, body 'TimeoutRejectedException: The operation did not complete within the allowed timeout of 00:00:30', elapsed exactly ~30.2-30.4s each time -- not a cold-start fluke, reproducible.

Diagnosed directly against Runtime's own GET /chat endpoint (bypassing the gRPC hop entirely): it ALSO failed at exactly ~30.1s with HTTP 500. This contradicted the earlier session's belief that this endpoint ran -- read ProjectName.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs and confirmed builder.Services.ConfigureHttpClientDefaults(http => http.AddStandardResilienceHandler()) applies the framework's default 10s-attempt/30s-total resilience timeout to EVERY HttpClient in both processes (the Ollama API client in Runtime AND the gRPC channel in OrchestrationApi), and that the earlier per-client override -- builder.Services.Configure<HttpStandardResilienceOptions>('model-orchestrator', ...) in Runtime's Program.cs -- was still present on disk but evidently never took effect (the named-options key it targets does not match AddStandardResilienceHandler()'s actual internal pipeline-option name), so both hops were still running under the unmodified 30s default the whole time.

Fixed at the actual shared registration site instead of guessing another named-options key: parameterized http.AddStandardResilienceHandler(options => {...}) directly inside ConfigureHttpClientDefaults in ProjectName.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs (5-minute attempt/total timeout, 10-minute circuit-breaker sampling duration -- same values as the abandoned per-client attempt, now applied where they actually take effect for every client in both processes), and removed the now-redundant, non-functional per-client override and its now-unused Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience import from Runtime/Program.cs rather than leaving dead code. Ran dotnet build ProjectName.slnx -m:1: Build succeeded, 0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s). Restarted the AppHost fresh and re-ran both calls: GET /api/chat succeeded twice (12.48s -> {model:qwen3:8b,response:Hello.}, 16.51s -> {model:qwen3:8b,response:Hello!}), and GET Runtime's own /chat succeeded once (8.78s -> {model:qwen3:8b,response:Hello.}) -- all three real, live, Ollama-generated responses, no more 30s failures.

Terminated the AppHost and all child dotnet processes cleanly. git status showed only the two intended files (ProjectName.Runtime/Program.cs, ProjectName.ServiceDefaults/Extensions.cs) modified -- no stray state from the live run. Committed and pushed to origin.
